P: 1. Assess hydration and ability to tolerate oral rehydration; consider BMP when dehydration is significant and targeted stool testing for severe, persistent or bloody illness rather than routinely; educate about oral rehydration, hand hygiene and warning signs; recheck within 24–48 hours and use urgent care for inability to drink, scant urine, bloody stool or worsening focal pain. Wash hands with soap and water; avoid preparing food or caring for children until at least 48 hours after symptoms stop, following workplace/public-health rules.

2. Ask about recurrent episodes, nocturnal diarrhea, weight loss and blood; pursue stool inflammatory testing and gastroenterology evaluation only if persistent features support it; explain that current acute exposure makes infection more likely.

3. Reconcile antibiotics, laxatives and supplements; avoid unnecessary antibiotics and review any culprit medication with the prescriber; educate on medication-related diarrhea and arrange reassessment in 48–72 hours if symptoms persist despite recovery measures; consider targeted stool testing for persistent illness.

P: 1. Assess hydration and ability to tolerate oral rehydration; consider BMP when dehydration is significant and targeted stool testing for severe, persistent or bloody illness rather than routinely; educate about oral rehydration, hand hygiene and warning signs; recheck within 24–48 hours and use urgent care for inability to drink, scant urine, bloody stool or worsening focal pain. Explain oral rehydration in simple terms and have the patient describe a feasible drinking plan. Wash hands with soap and water; avoid preparing food or caring for children until at least 48 hours after symptoms stop, following workplace/public-health rules.

2. Ask about recurrent episodes, nocturnal diarrhea, weight loss and blood; pursue stool inflammatory testing and gastroenterology evaluation only if persistent features support it; explain that current acute exposure makes infection more likely.

3. Reconcile antibiotics, laxatives and supplements; avoid unnecessary antibiotics and review any culprit medication with the prescriber; educate on medication-related diarrhea and arrange reassessment in 48–72 hours if symptoms persist despite recovery measures; consider targeted stool testing for persistent illness.
